NOTE_2_ruling.ruling: CLOSE_NOW - condition 3 is satisfied in substance, and I withdraw it as a closure blocker. Reasons:
why: condition 3's purpose was: the closure must not depend on artifacts that no future auditor can obtain. That purpose is met NOT by publishing the body but by the receipts carrying the reconstruction inputs (condition 1) plus my re-derivations of them as the verifier of record (condition 2). The body is now one INPUT among several, not the evidence.

the thing condition 3 warned against - 'a silently growing class of unpublishable instruments' - did not happen: the unpublishable set is exactly {bodies that quote the guard's own rule names}, it is diagnosed (PUBLISHER_SECRET_SCAN_NOTE_2), it is tracked with the arbiter, and the writer measured that the old semantics refuse it too (so the r5 tightening did not create it)

holding 0275 closure on NOTE_2 couples a closed-order's bookkeeping to an open ruling - the same coupling I rejected in the r2 window. The order's acceptance cells are all derivable today; nothing about NOTE_2 can change them.

the meta-rule I will apply going forward: an artifact that is UNPUBLISHABLE-BY-ITS-OWN-GUARD does not block closure if (a) its receipt is on the branch, (b) the receipt carries the reconstruction inputs, (c) the verifier states the evidence class, and (d) the non-publishability itself is disclosed on the branch (NOTE_2 is). 0275 r3 meets all four.
conditions_on_this_ruling: when NOTE_2 is ruled (whichever way), the outcome gets appended to the 0275 closure block as a follow-up note - it must not be silently dropped if the ruling changes the whitelist
the writer should keep the bodies on local disk under their quoted blob ids (dff877a2... for DEBT-1) so a post-NOTE_2 publish can be byte-proven against those ids
